historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr, cross-checked against FY2026 guidance (+9-10%, refresh-cycle catch-up) and management's mid-single-digit long-term frame
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 10.0% vs revenue 5.6% (>30% divergence): equity growth is retained earnings on a shrinking share base, not a growth signal. EPS 3yr CAGR 30.8% and owner-FCF 3yr CAGR 58.9% both compound off the FY2022 trough (supply-chain cost inflation, $158m owner FCF) and are not repeatable; the 5yr figures are the informative ones.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF 5yr CAGR (10.4%) exceeds reported-FCF CAGR (8.6%): SBC grew only 2.8%/yr FY2020-25 (201.9 -> 231.5) while reported FCF grew 8.6%/yr, so SBC has been falling as a share of revenue (8.6% -> 7.5%). Growth here is not being paid for in stock.

scenario_narratives.base: F5 is a mature, net-cash ADC incumbent converting to subscription software. FY2026's guided 9-10% growth carries breach-recovery and refresh-cycle catch-up; the base case fades growth from 6% in FY2027 to 2.5% by FY2036 while adjusted EBITDA margin settles at 36.5% and SBC glides from 7.5% to 6% of revenue. The axes that matter are the durability of the BIG-IP refresh cycle, whether the AI data-centre insertion points scale beyond ~$100m, and how long the October 2025 nation-state breach weighs on federal and security-conscious buyers.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI inference security and data-delivery use cases (200%+ growth in H1 FY2026 off ~$50m) plus competitive displacement from Citrix/VMware sustain high-single-digit growth for four years; the subscription mix pushes adjusted EBITDA margin to 38% and SBC intensity falls to 5.5%. Terminal growth 3%, cap 20x.
scenario_narratives.bear: The hardware surge reverses in FY2027, the breach's reputational and litigation tail persists, and hyperscaler-native load balancing erodes the on-prem base; revenue is flat for two years and grows 2% thereafter, margin compresses to 32.5%, SBC holds at 7.8% of a stalled revenue base. Terminal growth 2%, cap 15x. No scenario hits the zero terminal floor: the business remains strongly cash-generative even in the bear case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF: SBC fully expensed (share count flat, buybacks value-neutral), interest income on the $1.6bn cash pile stripped and the cash added back once, margins built from components rather than carried forward from a peak year, cash tax at a normalised 22%. Terminal value is the lower of Gordon and a cap multiple (18x base), and the 15% hurdle entry price rebuilds its own terminal value at the hurdle rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: FY2026 growth (9-10%) includes refresh-cycle and post-breach catch-up; if the systems surge is cyclical rather than structural, FY2027-28 growth is at or below the bear path.
Breach long tail: federal re-certification, securities class action and derivative litigation, and reputational damage to a security vendor could depress bookings for longer than guidance implies.
Terminal value is a large share of value in every scenario; each 1pp of WACC or 0.5pp of terminal growth moves the base value materially (see sensitivity grid).
SBC intensity (7.6% of revenue) is the gap between house and street bases; the market price sits above even the street basis, implying it pays for growth beyond the base path.
Distributor concentration (~33% of revenue via two distributors) creates lumpiness in reported growth.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 223.76-462.0
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts API (CIK 1048695): 10-K FY2025 (year ended 2025-09-30) and 10-Q Q3 FY2026 (quarter ended 2026-06-30) for revenue, OCF, capex, SBC, interest income, shares, cash, leases, taxes; research/FFIV/Reports/FFIV_Metrics.csv for the FY2008-FY2025 annual history and CAGRs
data_sources.qualitative: research/FFIV/Reports/FFIV_Analysis.json (2026-09-28): breach timeline, FY2026 guidance progression 0-4% -> 7-8% -> 9-10%, Q4 FY2026 guide $870-890m, AI use-case disclosures, bull/bear points

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2026E = 9M FY2026 actual 2499.242 (10-Q to 2026-06-30) + Q4 FY2026 guidance midpoint 880 (range 870-890, given 2026-07-27). FY2026 closes 2026-09-30, two days after this valuation, so it is treated as FY0 and year 1 of the driver paths is FY2027.
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 (57.550m; basic 56.726m weighted, 56.826m on issue at 30 June 2026). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice. Buybacks (TTM $626m) are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation (cash-flow add-back), TTM to 2026-06-30 = FY2025 231.491 + 9M FY2026 193.535 - 9M FY2025 174.243. F5 tags no separate net-share-settlement withholding line (PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation absent), so sbc_incl_equity_taxes equals the add-back; any withholding cash is inside the repurchase line and is not double-counted.
inputs.fcf_basis: TTM to 2026-06-30. reported_fcf = OCF - capex = (949.666 + 841.373 - 741.598) - (43.26 + 63.705 - 27.119). interest_income = us-gaap:InterestIncomeOther TTM = 40.8 + 27.0 - 27.6. last_fcf = 969.595 - 250.783 - 40.2 (owner FCF).
inputs.buyback_basis: TTM PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock = FY2025 502.085 + 9M FY2026 501.109 - 9M FY2025 377.077; ~$500m/yr pace, actual financing outflow.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 4.5%, beta ~0.95 -> cost of equity ~8.5%. No debt (term loan repaid FY2023; no borrowings tagged since), so WACC = cost of equity = 8.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios; risk is carried in the driver paths and the weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases ($252.4m liability at 2026-06-30) are expensed inside operating income, so the lease cost is already in the EBITDA margin path. Lease liabilities are therefore NOT added to net debt and no lease_cost_pct_path is used (one treatment, not two).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 1: operating tech company; first valuation, no memory entry). Interest income is stripped because net cash ($1.61bn) is ~2.4x the owner-FCF base and is added back to EV. EBITDA margin path is PRE-SBC adjusted EBITDA (GAAP EBIT + D&A + SBC): FY2025 35.5%, 9M FY2026 34.9% (includes ~$17.5m+ cyber-incident costs). D&A includes ~$43m/yr acquired-intangible amortisation, so da_pct starts above capex_pct and converges to it. Cash tax: FY2025 cash taxes were 25.4% of pretax vs a 14.3% GAAP provision, inflated by Section 174 R&D capitalisation; OBBBA restored immediate expensing from 2025 so the cash rate is set at 21% for two years then 22% (21% federal + state). Data caveat: the Metrics CSV quarterly labels carry the XBRL fy/fp shift (the 'Q4 2025' row is Q1 FY2026 Oct-Dec 2025 revenue 822.465; the 'Q2 2026' row is Q3 FY2026 Apr-Jun 2026 with the 2026-06-30 balance sheet); all anchors here were re-read from the SEC companyfacts API by period start/end dates. Price is the Friday 2026-09-25 regular close, not after-hours.

bear.narrative: The FY2026 systems surge proves to be a post-breach and refresh catch-up: hardware normalises in FY2027-28, the breach's long tail (federal re-certification under ED-26-01, class-action settlement, customer churn to hyperscaler-native and Cloudflare-type alternatives) caps growth near zero for two years and 2% thereafter. Margin compresses 300bp on remediation spend and pricing pressure; SBC does not shrink with revenue.

base.narrative: FY2027 growth steps down from FY2026's guided 9-10% (which carries breach-recovery and BIG-IP refresh catch-up) to 6% and fades to 2.5% by year 10. Adjusted EBITDA margin recovers 60bp as cyber-incident costs roll off and the subscription mix rises, then holds at 36.5%. SBC glides 7.5% -> 6.0% of revenue. Working-capital capture 15% of revenue growth reflects deferred-revenue inflows netted against receivables/inventory on systems growth.

bull.narrative: AI data-centre delivery/security (CalypsoAI, ADSP) becomes a real second growth engine on top of a multi-year hardware refresh and competitive displacement from Citrix/VMware; high-single-digit growth persists for four years and software mix lifts adjusted EBITDA margin to 38%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the October 2025 breach is an unresolved single-event risk to a security vendor's core value proposition, with a live securities class action, a CISA emergency directive on the federal base, and two distributors at ~33% of revenue; a reversal of the FY2026 hardware surge is a plausible path, not a tail. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: the bull case needs AI security, the refresh cycle and margin expansion to all deliver together, and FY2026's raised guidance already embeds much of the recovery. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
